sections.question: Which Pension Schemes Act 1993 subsection did alpha's rule on transfer payments to other schemes cite from 1 April 2022?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source fact (Doc 1, Annex E, draft regulation 5): under the heading "Amendment of regulation 142 (transfer of payments made to other schemes or pension arrangements)", the draft reads "In regulation 142(4), for “95(2)” substitute “95(2A)”." So alpha's rule on transfer payments to other schemes is regulation 142, and before any change its paragraph (4) cited section 95(2).
Step 2. Source fact (Doc 1, paragraph 3.3): the change was proposed as an "amendment to regulation 142 to correct a cross reference to the wrong subsection" of the Pension Schemes Act 1993.
Step 3. Source fact (Doc 1, Annex E, draft regulation 1(2)): "These Regulations come into force on 1st April 2022". Had draft regulation 5 been made, the rule would have cited the substitute subsection from that date.
Step 4. Source fact (Doc 2, Cabinet Office response on the technical amendments): "Cabinet Office has decided not to proceed with the amendment of regulation 142 to update a cross-referencing error". The 2022 amendments therefore left regulation 142(4) unchanged.
Step 5. Conclusion (Doc 1 and Doc 2): from 1 April 2022 the rule still cited section 95(2) of the Pension Schemes Act 1993.
Decoy: 95(2A), the substitute subsection in Doc 1's draft regulation 5, never took effect, because Doc 2 records that the amendment of regulation 142 was not made.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Superseded date or version
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Superseded date or version: Doc 1's draft regulation 5 would change regulation 142(4) from 95(2) to 95(2A) from 1 April 2022. A careless solver assumes the draft took effect and answers 95(2A). Doc 2 paragraph 4.61 says the amendment was not made, so the rule still cited 95(2).
